channel.title: Merkle Street
channel.description: Merkle Street reports crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, layer 2s, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation, security incidents and protocol upgrades.

item.title: Why an XMR bridge may pause during destination maintenance
item.description: An XMR bridge can stop new transfers when its destination chain is under maintenance, while deposits and already submitted transactions follow separate steps.

item.title: How Arbitrage Rebalances Prices Across Token Pools
item.description: Arbitrageurs compare token pool prices, trade against gaps and account for fees, slippage and delay; their activity can align pools without guaranteeing equal prices.

item.title: How to Match a Two-Token Deposit Ratio on Blackhole Swap
item.description: A two-token liquidity deposit must match the pool’s value ratio; Blackhole Swap can convert surplus assets before you add both sides and receive pool shares.

item.title: How Much Liquidity Does a Treasury Swap Need?
item.description: A treasury swap needs enough active pool depth to keep price impact within policy; estimate it from route quotes, slippage limits and the assets left afterward.

item.title: Claim Pool Fees Without Removing Your Liquidity
item.description: A separate collect transaction can send earned tokens to your wallet while your liquidity stays in the pool, but the option depends on how the pool records fees.

item.title: A Base Swap Is the Trade; the Pool Is What Makes It Work
item.description: A swap is a trade; a pool supplies tokens and sets the price. See which fits a one-off trade, and what you take on when you provide liquidity.

item.title: What Happens When a Crypto Bridge’s Source Transaction Fails
item.description: A failed source transaction usually leaves bridge funds unmoved, but still costs gas; learn how to read the receipt and separate a revert from a stalled relay.

item.title: Why Wallet Network Data Goes Out of Date
item.description: A wallet’s network label and endpoint tell it where to read and send transactions; stale settings can show old balances, reject fees, or misdirect activity.

item.title: How a Same-Chain Stablecoin Swap Works
item.description: A same-chain stablecoin swap sends one token into a contract or pool and returns another, with price impact, fees and approvals shaping the amount received.

item.title: What to Do With an Unfilled Limit Order After a Swap
item.description: A swap can leave an order untouched when its price condition or available liquidity is not met; check its state, then keep, cancel, or reprice it deliberately.

item.title: How New Token Pool Seeding Creates a Market
item.description: Token pool seeding pairs a new asset with a quote token, sets its first market price and gives traders a pool to swap against, with liquidity risks to check.

item.title: When Should a Treasury Split a Cross-Chain Payment?
item.description: Splitting a cross-chain treasury payment can improve route capacity and limit exposure, but extra transactions add fees, timing gaps and reconciliation work.

item.title: How to Return Mantle Assets for an Exchange Deposit
item.description: To deposit Mantle-held crypto at an exchange, first check whether it accepts the Mantle network; otherwise withdraw through the bridge to a supported chain.

item.title: Recover a Manta Bridge Session After Disconnect
item.description: A wallet disconnect usually ends the page session, not a submitted transfer; reconnect the same account, check history and status, then resume the missing step.

item.title: Choose a Recipient Wallet That Can Receive on the Destination Chain
item.description: Choose a recipient wallet that supports the destination chain and token; verify its address format, any required memo, and the bridge route before sending.

item.title: Why BSC Token Charts Show Different Prices
item.description: BSC token charts can disagree because they follow different pools, quote assets or update rules. Check the token contract, pair liquidity and trade size before acting.

item.title: Three Checks Before a Treasury Bridge Transfer
item.description: A treasury bridge route is useful only when the asset arrives as intended, settles on schedule and fits the team’s controls for custody, liquidity and recovery.

item.title: How Polygon PoS State Sync Delivers a Deposit
item.description: Polygon PoS state sync carries an Ethereum deposit message through Heimdall to Bor, where a child-chain contract mints the matching token after the root asset is locked.

item.title: Rebalance Yield Vaults After Withdrawals in Five Steps
item.description: After a withdrawal, recalculate vault weights, account for pending assets, and rebalance in a controlled order so remaining depositors inherit a sound strategy.

item.title: A Cross-Chain Transfer Is Pending. What Should You Do?
item.description: A cross-chain transfer can wait on source-chain finality, bridge verification, or destination execution; check the stage before retrying or sending again.
